question:
(i) Explain why wave theory of light fails to explain the main observations of the photoelectric effect.
(ii) Explain how atomic line spectra also support the idea that energy exchange in atoms is quantised.

options.A:
(i) Wave theory explains threshold frequency and instantaneous emission using intensity alone.
(ii) Atomic spectra are continuous and do not support quantisation.
options.B:
(i) Wave theory fails only because it predicts electrons have no charge.
(ii) Atomic lines come from arbitrary electron energies.
options.C:
(i) Wave theory predicts maximum kinetic energy depends on intensity, agreeing with experiments.
(ii) Atoms emit every possible frequency because energy levels are continuous.
options.D:
(i) Wave theory fails to explain threshold frequency, instantaneous emission, and $K_{\max}$ depending on frequency rather than intensity. Photon theory explains these using $E=h u$ and $K_{\max}=h u-\phi_0$.
(ii) Atomic lines arise because electrons have allowed levels and transitions obey $h u=E_i-E_f$; both phenomena require quantised energy exchange.
